blinding_guess.why: A ships a unittest suite that covers each requirement, which hints at a more structured process, but both implementations are very similar.

notes: Both sides meet every stated requirement: all types, enum, bounds, lengths, patterns, dot-notation nested paths and reporting all errors at once, with identical error sets in P23. B also supports array 'items' with [n] indices and rejects unknown types and invalid regexes as schema errors (exit 2). A reports an invalid regex as a validation error (exit 1), which is acceptable. Both pass 32 of 35 probes but fail different ones: A has a silent unknown-type acceptance, and B has traceback crashes on malformed input. A's 9 unittest tests pass (run with unittest because pytest is not installed); B has no tests. Neither side has bandit findings in its validator code; A's bandit findings are all low and in its test subprocess calls.
